content.intro: This lesson covers Exploring the Rust Standard Library. It sits in Module 14, Standard Library, Files, and Input/Output, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Exploring the Rust Standard Library matters when you work with type-safe program design. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Exploring the Rust Standard Library, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. Use Path and PathBuf instead of manually joining path strings; handle I/O errors because filesystem conditions can change between checks and use.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the Rust sample as src/main.rs in a Cargo project and run cargo run. Review the expected output, then change one input to explore an edge case.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Return the sample to its original form, run the documented command again, and compare the result. If a dependency, target, runtime, database, or hardware device is required, configure that separately before treating the result as verified.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake and recovery
content_blocks.text: Do not assume Exploring the Rust Standard Library guarantees more than it actually does. Reduce a failure to a small reproducer, read the full compiler diagnostic or error value, consult the matching official reference, and change one assumption at a time.

content_blocks.title: Toolchain and execution boundary
content_blocks.text: Course examples are static reference snippets, not executed inside CodeLeaf. Most standard-library examples can be tried in a Rust 2024 Cargo project; specialized networking, database, async, procedural-macro, embedded, and WebAssembly scenarios require the toolchain and dependencies described in their lessons.
